transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Time: 15:00 - 15:49 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Orion Head of Security), Leah Park (Orion Cloud Ops), Samir Patel (Eng Manager), Nadia El-Amin (Compliance)

Summary:
Short review of Redwood's audit logging capabilities focused on admin activity, what fields are captured, export options, retention policies, and integration with customer SIEM/KMS. Customer wants clarity on retention and on-prem/exporting for regulatory audits.

Topics:
- What audit events are captured (admin logins, role changes, provisioning, API keys, model pinning, deletion)
- Export options (S3, syslog, streaming via webhook / ELK/Fluentd)
- Retention defaults and configurable retention + legal hold
- Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM integration for export keys
- RBAC/SSO correlation fields for traceability

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Turner: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Im Alex, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Maya, our security-focused SE.
[00:12] Maya Chen: hi all. let me know if i talk too fast i can slow down.
[00:18] Carlos Ramirez: thanks Alex, Maya. we're especially interested in audit logs and admin activity — need to understand exactly what you capture and how we can ship that to our SIEM for retention and audit.
[00:28] Alex Turner: absolutely. goal for today is to walk through the event taxonomy, export options, retention defaults, and KMS/encryption flows. we'll also show a sample export.
[00:39] Leah Park: good. we have retention constraints from our legal team — 7 years for admin actions for some funds — so we need to know if Redwood can hold for that long or if we need to export and store in-house.
[00:50] Maya Chen: short answer: hosted accounts have configurable retention up to X days by default and we provide exports — plus long-term retention via S3 export or streaming to your SIEM is supported. we'll go into details.
[01:05] Samir Patel: what's X days? and is that editable per-account?
[01:10] Maya Chen: default is 90 days in hosted by default, but for enterprise customers we support custom retention policies and legal hold. for Dedicated/Private installs you can set retention per environment.
[01:21] Nadia El-Amin: and for compliance evidence — do you include raw payloads or are they redacted? particularly we care about PII redaction for transcripts.
[01:30] Maya Chen: good callout. audit logs focus on metadata and admin activity — actions like admin login, role changes, API key creation/deletion, model version pinning, deployment rollouts, config changes, and export events. We include request identifiers and references to assets; we do not store full user-submitted data in the admin activity log by default. where payloads are needed for debug we mark them and access is controlled and audited.
[01:52] Carlos Ramirez: so login events, IP, user-id, role, timestamp — do we get session ids and MFA results?
[01:58] Maya Chen: yes. we capture user principal (SAML/SCIM id when available), session id, IP, user agent string, MFA result (success/failure), and the action outcome (success/error) plus an event id for cross-correlation.
[02:15] Alex Turner: i'll paste a sample export after the call; it contains event_name, event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, source_ip, user_agent, resource_type, resource_id, before/after for config changes, outcome, and request_id.
[02:32] Leah Park: great. on exports, you mentioned S3 — can we push directly to our locked S3 bucket and have server-side encryption with our CMK?
[02:40] Maya Chen: yes, we support pushing exports to your S3 using a customer-provided bucket or to our storage then forwarded. For direct-to-customer S3 we can do server-side encryption using your KMS CMK, or you can use SSE-S3. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and key imports.
[02:59] Samir Patel: do you do streaming in near-real-time for SIEM? we want low-latency ingest into Splunk/Datadog.
[03:07] Maya Chen: we have a streaming webhook option and connectors for common SIEMs; typical architecture is using Fluentd/Logstash or an event forwarder that subscribes to our audit stream. For very high volume we recommend the streaming endpoint which pushes events within a few seconds.
[03:22] Carlos Ramirez: how do you guarantee ordering or deduplication? sometimes replayed events confuse our analytics.
[03:28] Maya Chen: every event has an event_id + request_id + sequence number per session. for retries we include a retry_count and idempotency token so your collector can dedupe.
[03:37] Alex Turner: also we surface a change history for resources — e.g., when a role mapping changes you'll get before/after blobs that show previous role config and new role config as JSON diffs.
[03:50] Nadia El-Amin: we're regulated — SOC 2 and ISO — do you include audit log integrity features? immutability or append-only storage?
[03:59] Maya Chen: for enterprise we offer append-only logs backed by WORM (write once read many) storage on our Dedicated product and we can provide signed log digests for tamper-evidence. For hosted we provide strong access controls and retention policies; for attestation we can provide signed export bundles on request.
[04:17] Leah Park: do you support legal hold, like preventing deletion regardless of retention?
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes — legal hold flags prevent rollback/deletion while enabled. we keep the record and also can export an immutable bundle.
[04:28] Carlos Ramirez: on RBAC/SSO correlation — can you map SAML attributes into events? We rely on department and entitlements for tracing who did what.
[04:36] Maya Chen: we ingest SAML/SCIM attributes and include them in the actor metadata. common fields: saml_nameid, email, department, groups, external_id. you can also map custom attributes and we'll surface them in events.
[04:50] Samir Patel: what about API key rotations — if a key is rotated did you capture which service or user rotated it?
[04:56] Maya Chen: yes, an api_key_rotate event includes actor_id, key_id masked (last 4 chars), previous_key_id reference, and outcome.
[05:05] Alex Turner: quick note on privacy — we mask sensitive fields by default; the export schema documents which fields are redacted or hashed. if you need raw data for debugging there's an elevated access workflow with audit.
[05:18] Carlos Ramirez: okay. on export formats — JSON vs CSV — what's available?
[05:22] Maya Chen: we provide JSONL for streaming and S3 exports, CSV for simple ingestion, and parity schemas for both. JSONL preserves structured before/after diffs better.
[05:33] Leah Park: retention again — if hosted default is 90 days, but we need 7 years. what are options and cost implications?
[05:40] Maya Chen: enterprise customers typically export to their S3 cold storage and we can optionally retain short-term in our system for 90/180 days for quick lookup. Long-term retention is handled by your storage — cost is your S3/archival cost. Redwood can automate periodic exports (daily/weekly) and we offer lifecycle hooks to move to Glacier.
[05:58] Carlos Ramirez: do you provide retention labeling for different types of events? we might want admin actions kept longer than request traces.
[06:06] Maya Chen: yes, retention policy can be event-class based. admin_activity, auth_events, config_changes can each have different retention.
[06:15] Samir Patel: is there an option for on-prem archive if we can't store in cloud region due to residency?
[06:22] Maya Chen: for Private deployments yes; you can mount NFS or local object storage and configure exports to stay within your network. For hosted we support regional restrictions and direct-to-customer buckets in designated regions.
[06:34] Alex Turner: i'll note that we have customers running in EU regions and fips-enabled setups. Maya will follow up with configuration doc.
[06:42] Nadia El-Amin: about KMS integration — are keys rotated automatically? who manages the envelope keys vs data keys?
[06:49] Maya Chen: we follow envelope encryption patterns. For direct S3 exports with your CMK, you control the master key rotation schedule. For data at rest in Dedicated we can use your KMS or Redwood-managed keys. We support external HSMs for FIPS-compliant operations.
[07:05] Carlos Ramirez: any SLAs around log export delivery? if you push to our SIEM we need guarantees.
[07:12] Maya Chen: for streaming exports we have delivery SLAs on Dedicated plans. For hosted streaming we target <30s delivery but SLA depends on plan. We'll include specifics in the post-call doc.
[07:24] Samir Patel: curious — do you capture model-level events like model pinning or quantization changes? we need to know who changed a model config because it affects inference behavior.
[07:32] Maya Chen: yes. model_version_pin, model_quantize_toggle, rollout_start/complete are tracked with before/after and affected resource ids.
[07:41] Alex Turner: quick demo note: shared a sample export link in the chat (https://redwood.example.com/share/audit-sample-2026-04-02) — that's sanitized.
[07:52] Leah Park: got it. we'll validate schema with our SIEM team.
[07:56] Carlos Ramirez: what's the recommended ingest pattern to avoid bursts affecting Redwood throughput?
[08:01] Maya Chen: we recommend copying events into a buffer (SQS/Kinesis) and then process into SIEM. our streaming endpoint is rate-limited to protect production; for spikes we advise batching to S3 and asynchronous ingestion.
[08:14] Samir Patel: for compliance we'd like to see an example audit bundle for an incident response — can you produce a tamper-evident export with signatures?
[08:22] Maya Chen: yes, we can produce signed bundles with SHA256 digests and a signed manifest. that's part of our enterprise incident response package.
[08:31] Alex Turner: to recap next steps: we'll share the export sample and KMS integration doc, and propose a follow-up to validate schema against Orion SIEM.
[08:40] Nadia El-Amin: thanks. we'll confirm internal retention and get back to you.
[08:43] Carlos Ramirez: thanks all, that was helpful.

End of transcript.
